policy: Public methodology only. Encoded as review lenses a human (or SELF) must apply. Not a substitute for those firms' work.

tactics.title: Threat-model the system before the bytecode
questions: What are the trust boundaries (oracles, admin keys, keepers, bridges, off-chain signers)?
What is the economic model and who can move price or liquidity in one transaction?
What is the upgrade and incident-response path?
tactics.why: Most catastrophic failures live in architecture, not in a missing require.

tactics.title: Write protocol invariants and fuzz them
questions: What must remain true after every public call (solvency, k, share backing, message uniqueness)?
Are those statements encoded as Foundry/Echidna/Medusa invariants?
Do the invariants hold under donations, first deposit, and empty markets?
tactics.why: Surface scanners cannot see protocol-specific logic, which Immunefi says is now ~89% of DeFi losses.

tactics.title: Line-by-line plus contest-champion attack imagination
questions: For each external/public function: who can call it, what value moves, what state changes, what is called out?
What happens if this function is called twice, re-entered, or sandwiched?
What happens if a listed token is FoT, rebasing, ERC777, or Token-2022?
tactics.why: Pashov-style reviews treat every state-changing entry as an attack surface, not a happy path.

tactics.title: Checks-effects-interactions and initializer hygiene
questions: Is every external call after the last storage write that the callee can observe?
Are implementation initializers disabled in the constructor?
Does ERC-4626 use a decimals offset / virtual shares?
tactics.why: Wintermute-class init and 4626 inflation still appear in 2025 contest reports.

tactics.title: Review the integration, not only the new file
questions: Which external protocols are trusted for price, share rate, or message validity?
If that protocol is paused, upgraded, or re-entered, what happens here?
Are callbacks (flash loan, hooks, harvest, migrate) authenticated?
tactics.why: Penpie, Prisma zap, and Harvest all failed at the integration boundary.

tactics.title: Empty-vault and donation inflation is still High/Med every contest
questions: What is convertToShares(1) when totalSupply is 0 and after a raw transfer of 1e18 + 1?
Does a wrapper vault inherit the underlying vault's inflation?
Is rounding always against the user on mint and in favor of the vault on burn?
tactics.why: Pareto 2025, BakerFi 2024, Burve 2025 and dozens of siblings.

tactics.title: Assume generic classes are patched; hunt protocol logic
questions: What is this protocol's unique state machine (migrate, harvest, donate, hook, zap)?
Which function was added after the last audit (Euler eIP-14 pattern)?
Can an attacker combine two intended features into an unintended profit?
tactics.why: Flash-loan-as-primary-vector is now marginal. Remaining losses are protocol-specific.

tactics.title: Search prior findings on the same primitive
questions: Has this exact function shape (onFlashLoan, harvest, convertToShares, processMessage) been exploited?
Which C4/Sherlock issues match the inheritance tree (Aave-fork, Compound-fork, 4626, CLAMM)?
tactics.why: Most 'new' bugs are known bugs on a renamed contract.

tactics.title: Stale + sequencer + heartbeat on every price read
questions: Is latestRoundData checked for answeredInRound, updatedAt, and non-zero answer?
On L2, is the sequencer-uptime feed consulted?
Is there a protocol heartbeat independent of the feed?
tactics.why: A 'fresh' timestamp during sequencer downtime is a frozen price.

tactics.title: Every remaining account is attacker-controlled
questions: Is every privileged account Signer or a PDA with canonical bump?
Are mutable pairs required to be distinct?
Is the token program / mint / sysvar typed rather than AccountInfo?
tactics.why: Cashio, Wormhole Solana path, and most Anchor contest Highs.

tactics.title: Treat the public mempool as an adversary
questions: Does every value-changing swap have minOut and a deadline?
Can initialize, first deposit, or commit be front-run?
Are liquidations and oracle updates sandwichable against users?
tactics.why: Missing slippage is still a daily extraction, even when it is not a 'hack'.

tactics.title: Audit the diff that shipped after the last report
questions: Which functions were added since the last audit (donate, migrate, hook, harvest)?
Does the new path skip a check the old paths still perform?
Did storage layout and initializer version increment correctly?
tactics.why: Euler's vulnerable function was introduced by a post-audit governance upgrade.

tactics.source: C4 2022-2025 replay of BakerFi, Next Generation, Revert Lend, Fraxlend, Ethena
tactics.title: Ask what each argument binds, not whether the project has a check somewhere
questions: Is domainSeparator / token / minOut / deadline a caller argument or computed on-chain?
Does every swap path set amountOutMinimum, or only one helper?
Does the oracle scale this feed's decimals(), or a hardcoded 1e18 from another file?
Does whitelist/blacklist wrap burn and redeem, or only transfer?
Does liquidate write off leftover debt, or only seize collateral?
tactics.why: Ten Code4rena high-bounty contests were missed when facts were OR-ed across the repo. A nonce in file A does not bind a signature in file B.

tactics.title: Read the brief before the bytecode
questions: What did the sponsor list under Known Issues / Automated Findings?
Which files are in scope.txt versus out_of_scope.txt?
Which roles are documented as trusted, and is that trust actually enforced in code?
Did the sponsor accept first-depositor inflation, FoT-incompatibility, or oracle-operator risk?
tactics.why: Ten C4 replays with --no-docs on scope-only copies ignored the contest README. Wardens are scored against that brief; repeating a declared known issue is wasted work, and reporting on an out-of-scope mock is a false positive.
